prompts.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: a high-quality landscape 3:2 teaching illustration for a Grade 7 Geography lesson comparing weather and climate. Original imagined coastal countryside, not a named place. Two equal side-by-side illustrated panels separated by a narrow ivory gutter, aligned views of the SAME small hill, red-roof cottage, tree and weather station. LEFT panel headed exactly 'WEATHER' with a smaller subtitle 'One day': close view of this place on a rainy windy day, clouds and diagonal rainfall, a small thermometer and windsock; a single daily calendar card with one day visibly circled (no invented date, temperature or numbers). RIGHT panel headed exactly 'CLIMATE' with a smaller subtitle 'Patterns over many years': the same landscape appears as four small beautifully composed seasonal vignettes in one coherent panel (spring green, summer warm, autumn foliage, winter cool), behind a clean stack of year-calendar pages and a simple long-term pattern line without numbers or axis claims. Bottom caption LEFT exactly 'Conditions now'; bottom caption RIGHT exactly 'Long-term patterns'. Scientifically accurate teaching message: weather concerns conditions at one time and place; climate concerns long-term patterns and variation. Do not imply climate never changes or that one day's observations establish a climate. Refined hand-painted educational illustration with accurate readable infographic elements: ivory background, navy labels, teal blue weather, muted green scenery, warm gold highlights. Spacious simple composition appropriate to a classroom projector; restrained details, very readable brief English lettering. No app UI, no buttons, no people, no mountains or rain shadow, no fake quantitative data, no watermarks. Both panels visually balanced and coherent; prioritize memorability and the difference in observation time scales.

Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: landscape 3:2 illustrated teaching diagram for Grade 7 Geography explaining why a mountain's leeward side may be drier. Draw one coherent, large, beautiful side-on mountain landscape cross-section. Ocean at far left, green wet windward slope on left, rocky mountain peak near center, descending leeward slope on right with drier muted gold fields and sparse vegetation, not an extreme barren desert. Make the mountain separate wet and drier sides clearly. One thick teal airflow arrow starts over ocean at left, flows LEFT TO RIGHT, rises smoothly along the LEFT slope to the summit, then descends along the RIGHT slope. Moist incoming air from sea on left, clouds and visible rain falling on the LEFT windward slope; smaller thinner clouds on right, no heavy rain there. Clear accurate simple teaching labels only: 'Moist air from the sea' on far left, 'Air rises and cools' above left slope, 'Clouds and rain' next to rainy left cloud, 'Windward side' beneath green left slope, 'Air descends and warms' above right slope, 'Leeward side' beneath right slope, 'Rain shadow: often drier' by right-side dry field. Small footer exactly 'The leeward side can still receive rain.' Airflow must be visibly continuous from left to right, arrows point UP and right on the windward slope and DOWN and right on leeward slope. Do not show arrows rising on right, do not show rain over leeward area, do not imply mountains create water. Scientific accuracy and readability are essential. Style refined naturalistic hand-painted classroom infographic, cohesive warm ivory background, navy lettering, teal arrows and ocean, muted green vegetation and warm ochre right slope, soft natural light. Mountain fills the composition with plenty of space around labels. No UI, no buttons, no people, no cars, no town labels, no dates, no invented numbers, no watermark. Labelled conceptual illustration of an imagined landscape, not evidence about a named location.
